item.title: Halide Witness
item.description:
On Film

My first ever camera was a 1973 Yashica Electro GSN. I found it in a Goodwill bin with the factory leather case. In the next bin down, I found the original lens screw-on accessories. I paid about $15 for the whole set. It was in pristine exterior condition, the lens attachments were even in their original plastic wrap within the leather holder. The only issue I could find was that the whole thing smelled like it had been hot boxed by cheap cigarrettes for the last 40 years. As I was wiping it down with towels and water, a thick yellow layer came off that smelled gross. The strap, the leather wrap, the satin chrome finish, every part was wiped down then left in the sun for a few hours to let the UV do some magic. Eventually it didn’t smell like a smoker’s toothbrush and I loaded some film into it. The first roll came back riddled with accidental double exposures and feed issues. Despite running into the Yashica’s dreaded Pad of Death issue (a well documented report of this by the Yashica guy here), the black and white images of that first roll were nothing short of magical to me. Little did I know that I had just unlocked my next obsession in the coming years.

item.title: The Pursuit of Almost
item.description:
10 months

I recently welcomed my first child to the world, got a new job, and moved across the country, all within the course of 4 months. I had set up a Dell Optiplex with a Ubuntu Server OS and a few home media server docker containers, including Jellyfin, the *arr suite, and a few other items for me to tinker around on. After the move, I unpacked that machine and it has since lain dormant inside of my organizer, unplugged and unmaintained. I’ve finally gotten around to plugging it in and beginning the update and maintenance process, but as I was getting everything fired up for the first time, I asked myself, “Why has it taken you so long to do something that comes nearly as naturally as breathing?”
